1.explanation:
• GroupBehavior.js: this is where new CategoryValue instances are created on group.create. Its getDefinitions() call returns the wrong parent when you’re inside a collapsed subprocess plane, so the created category isn’t added to the global Definitions._
• CategoryUtil.js: the createCategoryValue() helper actually adds your new Category/CategoryValue under the Definitions you pass in. If you hand it the wrong Definitions, nothing ends up in rootElements and the importer later can’t resolve the reference._
• BpmnImporter.js: this is where unresolved references are detected and logged. The _getElement() lookup fails for your stray CategoryValue and triggers the warning you see._
• SubProcessPlaneBehavior.js: this behavior sets up the “subprocess plane” root element when you drill down into a collapsed subprocess. Because it wires a different rootElement into canvas, GroupBehavior.getDefinitions() picks up the plane’s businessObject instead of the actual Definitions, causing the misplaced category._
1.bug_scenario: When you drill into a collapsed subprocess and add a Group shape there, on save the GroupBehavior creates a new bpmn:CategoryValue and hooks it up to the Group, but—because you’re working inside a subprocess plane—the new Category (and its CategoryValue) don’t end up in the right Definitions rootElements. On re-import, the importer can’t find that CategoryValue by ID and emits “unresolved reference <CategoryValue_…>”.
